claim: PAA-CPR ranks 12 global asset classes monthly by MOM=close/SMA(13 month-end closes)-1; if fewer than 7 of 12 have MOM>0, allocates the shortfall proportionally (CP%=(12-n)/6, or 100% if n<=6) to whichever of IEF/SHY has the higher MOM, holding the top-6-by-MOM equally in the remainder.
quote: If n <= 6, then allocate the entire portfolio to the CP asset, otherwise CP % = [(12 – n ) / 6]. More on the CP asset in a moment. If n >= 7 (or put another way, if CP % < 100%), select the 6 asset class with the highest MOM value, and allocate 1/6 of the remaining portfolio to each at the close.
limitations: AllocateSmartly's practitioner replication of Keller & Keuning's SSRN 2759734 paper; the site's own default backtest substitutes a synthetic cash rate for SHY in its current tracking, but confirms SHY as the original paper's own choice, which this batch uses.
independent_replication: AllocateSmartly has tracked PAA in near real time since around 2016; JW Keuning's own TrendXplorer blog independently discusses the same strategy.
impact_on_spec: Fixes candidate keller_keuning_paa_cpr_ssrn_2016_allocatesmartly_replication's rule, universe and parameters exactly as published, before any Sharpe or return number is computed for it in this batch's screening pass.
